answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it may submit bids, with deposits slashed when bonded peers prove fraud through a challenge window. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital and risk losing it; splitting a stake across aliases does not multiply influence. A relic auction might price quartz under umber rules, yet the same bond requirement applies to every bidder, making Sybil control costly rather than impossible.
